items.evidence: Notes never mention the project manager opening the meeting or stating the agenda; only 'The project lead and three team members reviewed a television remote-control design.'

'75% said remotes were ugly; 80% would pay more for a fancier-looking one', 'More than half cited losing remotes', 'People use about 10% of available buttons; channel and volume changes dominate', 'Voice-recognition interest fell with age'.

'The technical-functions presentation recommended balancing conventional controls with distinctive design... Prototype user interfaces could be tested for feedback.' Covers how to design one, but not the explanation of how a remote works (a communication device sending messages to the TV), and the presenter is not named.
'A fully featured remote is harder to learn; a basic remote omits functions.'
'The working-design presentation mapped the remote's key components... energy source, user interface, chip, and infrared bulb.' (presenter role not named)
'The project lead narrowed the product to television use, excluded teletext...' plus sections on target market, voice recognition, lost-remote function and battery/cradle.
'The team was asked to complete a questionnaire and summary after the meeting.'
'Individual work was allocated across industrial design, user interface, and market-trend watching.'
'Add the meeting minutes and presentation slides to the project documentation (owner: Speaker 1)'; summary: 'The project lead will add the minutes and slides to project documentation.'
The PM's request that everyone also post their documentation is not stated; notes only report one member had already placed a presentation in the shared folder.
'Individual work was allocated across industrial design... Each area had a corresponding concept or work focus.' The components concept is not named.
'Individual work was allocated across... user interface... Each area had a corresponding concept' - the user interface concept is only implied.
'Individual work was allocated across... market-trend watching.'
'The group will not design for teletext because the internet has taken its place.'
'The product will focus on television rather than video and other uses.'
'kept the company's recognizable colors and slogan in scope'; 'yellow and black and the slogan ... informing its look.'
'The group named simplicity, fashion, and usability as project priorities.'

'The group did not settle on an age-defined target market' and 'considered defining the audience by needs or spending ability rather than age alone' - does not state the conclusion to define objectives (fashion, simplicity) instead of an age group.
'The team agreed that a lost-remote finding function would address a frequently reported frustration.'
'large accessible essential buttons'
'access to extra functions'
'Extra controls should be less prominent or tucked away.'
'The group raised long battery life and a rechargeable cradle as possibilities.' The PM said 'that's a good idea, we'll keep it', but the notes present it only as a possibility.
'The target demographic remained open... Suggestions ranged from ages 15-35 to under 65 and 20-55.'
'The €12.50 production limit made voice recognition seem costly... The team questioned whether voice recognition was needed in a remote.'
The discussion of how to make infrared more functional (battery, chip quality) is absent; only 'reliable signal' appears in the presentation summary.
'battery life and charging remained design considerations'; 'long battery life and a rechargeable cradle'.
